sentences.text: This bipedal dinosaur moved on powerful legs with reduced arms.
Its skull featured a prominent ridge-like horn on the snout and a pair of horns above the eyes, reaching a maximum length of 79 cm in the largest known specimen.
The tail consisted of approximately 50 vertebrae and made up about half of the animal's total length.
The Cleveland-Lloyd specimen represents one of the largest-known Ceratosaurus specimens.
A Ceratosaurus skeleton was bought by a private museum and has not been scientifically described.
A life-sized model of Ceratosaurus appeared in the 1914 film Brute Force, which is possibly the first live-action dinosaur film.
If the horn was used for display, it was likely brightly colored.
The genus Ceratosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1884 based on a nearly complete skeleton found in Garden Park, Colorado, within the Morrison Formation.
The holotype specimen was discovered and excavated by farmer Marshall Parker Felch in 1883 and 1884.
A significant Ceratosaurus skeleton was discovered in the early 1960s by James Madsen and his team in the Cleveland-Lloyd Dinosaur Quarry in Utah.
Donald Henderson suggested in 1998 that Ceratosaurus used its long teeth as fangs for quick, slashing bites with concentrated force due to its narrow skull.
Snively and Russell suggested in 2007 that Ceratosaurus could make powerful upward and sideways head movements.
A 2026 study argues that the dentition of Ceratosaurus might have been an adaptation for quickly killing middle-sized prey.

Pathological evidence in Ceratosaurus includes a stress fracture in a foot bone and a broken tooth showing signs of further wear after the break, findings examined by Bruce Rothschild and others in 2001.
Ceratosaurus was a rare member of the theropod fauna, found at an average rate of 7.5 to 1 compared to Allosaurus in sites where both species coexist.
Ceratosaurus gives its name to the clade Ceratosauria, which diverged early from the lineage leading to modern birds.
Madsen and Welles described two new Ceratosaurus species, C. dentisulcatus and C. magnicornis, in a 2000 monograph.
The species name dentisulcatus refers to parallel grooves on the inner sides of certain teeth.
Brooks Britt and colleagues suggested in 2000 that C. nasicornis is a juvenile and the other species represent adults of the same species.
Researchers suggest that Ceratosaurus and other large theropods like Torvosaurus and Allosaurus occupied different ecological niches to reduce competition.
Portuguese Ceratosaurus bones were found in sandstones thought to be late Kimmeridgian in age.

It is debated whether the nasal horn was a weapon or used solely for display, with recent studies suggesting it was for display, though Marsh considered the nasal horn a powerful offensive and defensive weapon in 1884, a view agreed upon by Gilmore in 1920.
While some paleontologists suggested Ceratosaurus hunted aquatic prey like fish, this hypothesis has been rejected by more recent studies.
Some authors question whether any finds from the Tendaguru Formation belong to Ceratosaurus due to a lack of diagnostic features.
